description: Indium is a silvery-white post-transition metal and one of the softest elements with atomic number 49. It is highly ductile with a bright luster and so soft that it can be cut with a knife. Chemically, its properties are largely intermediate between gallium and thallium.
uses: Indium is used primarily in the production of flat-panel displays as indium tin oxide (ITO), a transparent and conductive coating. It is also used in the semiconductor industry in low-melting-point metal alloys such as solders and soft-metal high-vacuum seals, and in the manufacture of blue and white LED circuits.
characteristics: Indium has a Mohs hardness of 1.2, a melting point of 156.60 °C, and a boiling point of 2072 °C. It has a density of 7.31 g/cm³, becomes a superconductor below 3.41 K, and displays greater solubility in liquid mercury than any other metal. When bent, it produces a high-pitched crackling sound due to crystal twinning.
